subject: AtlasBank — scenario-driven breach analysis: sidecar provenance & KV cache isolation
messages:
From: Tom Langley <tom.langley@atlasbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@atlasbank.com, Emily Park <emily.park@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Request: scenario-based breach analysis and artifacts

Irene —

Thanks for taking this. Atlas Bank is putting Redwood through a scenario-driven security review focused on multi-tenant inference risks. We want a concise packet of artifacts and short write-ups that address the following: 

- Attack scenarios (brief): sidecar compromise that tries to exfiltrate KV cache or model context, cross-tenant inference leakage, and lateral movement from a worker to control plane components.
- Network/evidence: annotated topology diagram showing tenant/sidecar boundaries, per-tenant egress paths, ACLs, and bastion/egress control points.
- Provenance & telemetry: what traces/timestamps/headers prove request origin and how is KV cache access attributed to a tenant?
- Demonstration material: a pseudo packet-capture or red-team style log showing a simulated exfil attempt and how it is detected/blocked.
- Policies/evidence: where are ACLs documented, and can you provide a short spreadsheet listing control mappings (who/what/where) and retention windows.

Deliverables can be high-level (annotated diagram + explanation) with one technical appendix. Timeline: can you confirm if you can produce an initial packet by next week (target: 2026-12-07)? We also want a short (60m) call to walk through scenarios with our architects.

Thanks — appreciate a pragmatic, scenario-focused packet over a long questionnaire.

Tom Langley
Security Architect, Atlas Bank
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Langley <tom.langley@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: scenario-based breach analysis and artifacts

Tom —

Thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Jordan (solutions architect), Priyom (security PM), and Vanessa from Customer Success so we can assemble a targeted packet. High level plan:

1) Jordan will produce annotated attack-path diagrams (sidecar <-> KV cache <-> model runtime), and a pseudo-PCAP showing a simulated exfil attempt.
2) Priyom will draft a short control mapping (ACLs, egress controls, KMS usage, and retention) — spreadsheet attached as baseline.
3) Vanessa will prepare a one-page executive summary for your procurement team.

Attachments included: redwood-inference-topology-v2.vsdx (annotated topology) and egress-and-acls-evidence.xlsx (control mapping stub).

Questions / clarifications:
- Scope: do you need evidence for the last 90 days of logs, or a reproducible simulation is sufficient for your security review?
- Compliance tie-ins: should we also include the SOC 2 section references or do you already have that from our compliance portal?

Proposed next steps: we can run the 60-minute walkthrough on 2026-12-03; if that works for you we’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-read. Target deliverable date for the initial packet: 2026-12-07. If you need earlier, say so and we’ll prioritize the pseudo-PCAP and summary first.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tom Langley <tom.langley@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: scenario-based breach analysis and artifacts

Tom / team —

Quick technical clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need:

- KV cache segregation: caches are per-tenant namespaces backed by memory regions on the inference worker. Access to a tenant namespace is gated by the per-request tenant token validated in the sidecar before any KV read/write. Sidecar identity is mTLS-authenticated to the local runtime; there is no cross-tenant shared in-memory table.

- Sidecar compromise scenario: if a sidecar process is compromised, the principal risk is stolen tenant tokens and in-memory KV snapshots. We mitigate via: short-lived request tokens, KV writes encrypted at rest with tenant-wrapped KMS keys, and automatic prefix evictions when anomalous access patterns are detected.

- Network controls: worker outbound egress flows go through egress NATs in the tenant zone; control plane inter-service calls are on a private mesh with explicit ACLs. We can annotate the NATs and ACLs on the diagram.

- Demonstration materials: I will attach a synthetic sidecar-communication-sequence.txt that shows the sequence (client -> sidecar -> runtime -> KV read -> response) and a simulated pcap excerpt (redacted). The pcap will be a synthetic capture showing an attempted large KV dump which is blocked by rate/size guards and flagged by our telemetry.

I’ll own the attack-path diagrams and the synthetic pcap. Priyom, please confirm the retention window for control-plane audit logs we should reference for Atlas.

Attachment: sidecar-communication-sequence.txt (text stub).

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Langley <tom.langley@atlasbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@atlasbank.com>, security@atlasbank.com
Date: 2026-12-02T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: scenario-based breach analysis and artifacts

Irene / Jordan —

This is great; thank you. A few follow-ups:

- Demonstration: the synthetic pcap will be enough for our architecture review, but procurement also wants an example event that maps to an alert (i.e., sample telemetry + rule that would have triggered). Can you include the alert rule text and the telemetry fields?

- Logs: we do require the last 90 days of control-plane audit logs for the tenant provisioning/deprovisioning flows. If you can provide a hash + storage pointer (or the SOC2 control reference if logs are in the compliance portal) that will help.

- Data protection: please ensure the deliverable includes how KV at-rest encryption is applied per-tenant (KMS wrapping) and whether Redis/LMDB snapshots are ever written unencrypted to disk.

- Schedule: 60m walkthrough on 2026-12-03 at 16:00 PST — can you send a calendar invite?

We’ll also have a member of our legal/procurement team on the call; Vanessa, please keep an eye out for any procurement-level artifacts that may be needed (attestation, timelines for log handover, etc.).

Tom
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Langley <tom.langley@atlasbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: scenario-based breach analysis and artifacts — call confirmed & owners

Tom / Atlas team —

Call confirmed for 2026-12-03 16:00 PST. Calendar invite sent separately. Deliverable owners and immediate plan: 

- Jordan Blake: annotated attack-path diagrams + synthetic pcap + alert rule text (deliverable by 2026-12-07).
- Priyom Das: control mapping spreadsheet updated with KMS/WAL info, retention mapping, and pointer to control-plane audit logs or SOC2 control references (deliverable by 2026-12-07).
- Vanessa Ortiz: customer-facing one-pager and procurement checklist; will pull legal/procurement artifacts and coordinate any required attestation.

We will include: an explicit statement on KV at-rest encryption (tenant-wrapped keys via KMS), confirmation that no unencrypted snapshots are stored persistently, and a short appendix describing how token provenance is validated end-to-end.

Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3471 — we will attach the final artifacts to that ticket and post the diagram to the Drive link below.

Drive pre-read (internal): https://drive.google.com/file/d/diagram_atlas_v2

If anything changes before the call, I’ll update the thread. Looking forward to the walkthrough.

Best —
Irene Choi
Senior Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
